Sha'fu sat on the beach. For three days they had camped on the shoreline. Sha'fu had dug a fire pit, gathered wood, and lit a large fire. He had hung a tarp, and covered the floor in palm leaves. As campsites went, this was nice. He had hunted fish in the rock pools, and gathered nuts in the forest. For the first time in ages, Sha'fu had relaxed. The old Hag had gathered supplies, then placed a large cauldron upon the fire.

The Hag had then begun to make a potion, with the fruit from the heart. At first Sha'fu was alarmed, but the Hag had convinced him, that the goddess wanted it so. And so, for two days, the Hag had brewed the potion, often nipping off, to Hom knows where, to gather ingredients. It was on one such foray, that the old bird, had stumbled back with Kirtahs. The young male Shryke, was quite shaken. They had fed him, and seen to his injuries. It had pleased Sha'fu, to see a new face, to hear a new voice.

On the third day, the old Hag had proclaimed, "it's done!" He had taken out three large vials, and carefully decanted, all of the potion into them. Three vials of crystal clear liquid, "more valuable than gold and silver", the old Hag had said. It was on that evening, that Sha'fu sat in the sand. Kirtahs was scratching in that journal of his, while the old Hag told him tales. Tales of the roost, of beasts of the forest. Tales of the Gods themselves. He told Kirtahs, of the magic of Umbralocht, and how to summon it, at great personal cost. The two jabbered incessantly, Sha'fu expected them to go on late into the evening. Damn he could kill for a beer about now. A beer of the burrows, cold and bitter.

He stared out at the sea. A golden light, fading behind a darkening curtain of blue. Sunset, oh how Sha'fu loved to watch the sea eat the sun. He wished he could share this, with his brethren. He wished he could bring them here, to make burrows in the bluffs. Homes overlooking the ocean, with its cool breeze in the evening. God he could taste that beer. "Sha'fu!" Cried Kirtahs.

Sha'fu ducked and rolled. A life time of instincts kicked into gear. A moment later, a spear whizzed past, where his head had been, not a second ago. As Sha'fu rolled, he could see the Hag take a spear to the chest. "No!", he roared. He rolled to his feet, and dived left. A blurring spear, following, attacking his shadow. He rolled again, and ran for the tarp, dodging left and right. A spear kissed his ear, drawing blood, but not his life. He rolled again, under the tarp, and came up with his blade. He pirouetted and his blade met another.

He backed away, his sword blocking spear thrust, and counter thrust. Left and right, his sword meeting a maelstrom, a whirring maelstrom of death. There were two, two assailants. Sha'fu began to take stock, his instincts having kept him alive, his soldiers mind began to assess. The Hag was down. There were two creatures attacking him, and another had Kirtahs pinned. "Who are you?", Sha'fu growled. "[Sa'vak](http://ultraimg.com/images/image16f27.jpg)" spat his assailant.

As the word left the creatures mouth, his companion attacked. Spear blurring through the air, Sha'fu rolled. He rolled forward, under the spear, then twisted, his blade slashing across the creature belly. He was off at a run, before him was Kirtahs, pinned by one of the creatures. He jabbed for its neck, severing an artery, then Sha'fu rolled. Again he lived by an inch. "Run! Run Kirtahs!", he screamed. He blocked again, his sword moving like a whip, facing a blur, metal hitting metal, metal hitting wood. Sha'fu dodging and moving, staying alive before the maelstrom.

He fainted right, ducked left, then rolled. He ran again, this time for the Hag. Something hit him. Something was wrong, Sha'fu couldn't breath. Had something winded him. No. He stumbled forward, there in the soft golden sand, lay his friend, the old Hag. Sha'fu fell to his knees, his poor friend. He could feel something slide out from his chest, his side felt warm. His sword left his hand, falling in the soft golden sand. Something pierced his back again, a blade protruding from his chest. Sha'fu fell to the sand, his head turned towards his friend. The last thing he would ever see, was a snake like creature, take three vials, from the body of the Hag.
